dervis-irab:14-17.t:
* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوْا قَوْماً غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ): a resumptive statement brought to express wonder at the state of the hypocrites, who used to take the Jews as allies, giving them counsel and divulging the secrets of the believers to them. Al-Suddī said: "It has reached us that it was revealed about ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nufayl, one of the hypocrites." The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); لم is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and jussive; تر is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت"; إلى الذين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تر; the clause تولوا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position, and the wāw is the fāʿil; قوما is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause غضب الله عليهم is a naʿt (adjective) of قوما.
(ما هُمْ مِنْكُمْ وَلا مِنْهُمْ): the clause is resumptive, or a second adjective of قوما, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of تولوا. ما is the Ḥijāzī negating ما, هم is its noun and منكم its predicate; ولا: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negating; منهم is conjoined to منكم.
(وَيَحْلِفُونَ عَلَى الْكَذِبِ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; يحلفون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the clause is conjoined to تولوا, so it falls within the scope of the ṣila; على الكذب is a ḥāl; the wāw is circumstantial; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause يعلمون is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl.
(أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ عَذاباً شَدِيداً إِنَّهُمْ ساءَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; and إنّ with its noun and its predicate.
(اتَّخَذُوا أَيْمانَهُمْ جُنَّةً فَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): the clause is resumptive, or a third adjective of قوما, or a ḥāl. اتخذوا is a past verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; أيمانهم is the first mafʿūl bihi and جنة the second mafʿūl bihi of اتخذوا, i.e. a cover and protection for themselves and their property. فصدّوا: the fāʿ is conjunctive and صدّوا is a past verb with its fāʿil; عن سبيل الله is attached to صدّوا.
(فَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ): the fāʿ is conjunctive; لهم is a fronted khabar, عذاب a postponed mubtadaʾ, and مهين an adjective of عذاب, i.e. possessing humiliation.
(لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوالُهُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً): لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; تغني is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by لن; عنهم is attached to تغني; أموالهم is the fāʿil; ولا أولادهم is conjoined to أموالهم; من الله is attached to تغني with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "from the punishment of Allah"; and شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. even a little of availing.
(أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and أصحاب النار its khabar; هم is a mubtadaʾ, فيها is attached to خالدون, and خالدون is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The scholars of rhetoric have mentioned four views on the definition of truth and falsehood:
1- That truth is the conformity of the statement's judgement to reality, and falsehood its non-conformity to it, even if the belief [of the speaker] is otherwise in both cases.
2- This is the view of al-Naẓẓām, one of the great Muʿtazilites: that truth is conformity to the belief of the informant, even if mistaken, and falsehood is non-conformity to the belief, even if correct. [A statement made] with no belief accompanying it falls, on this view, within falsehood; there is no intermediate category.
3- This is the view of al-Jāḥiẓ, also one of the masters of the Muʿtazila: that truth is conformity to external reality together with the informant's belief in that conformity, and falsehood is non-conformity to reality together with the belief in its non-conformity; anything other than that is neither truth nor falsehood, i.e. an intermediate between them. This comprises four cases: the conforming with no belief in anything; the conforming with a belief in non-conformity; the non-conforming with a belief in conformity; and the non-conforming with no belief.
4- This is the view of al-Rāghib; it is like the view of al-Jāḥiẓ, except that he described the four cases as true and false under two considerations: truth in respect of conformity to external reality or to belief, and falsehood in respect of the absence of conformity to external reality or to belief.
Al-Naẓẓām adduced as proof the saying of Allah the Exalted: «إن المنافقين لكاذبون», i.e. in their saying «إنك لرسول الله», because it did not conform to their belief. His argument was refuted on the grounds that what is meant is that they are liars in the testimony, i.e. in their claim that the heart agrees with the tongue, since their saying "إنك ..." etc. implies "our testimony is from the depths of the heart", and this is a lie.
Al-Jāḥiẓ adduced as proof the saying of Allah the Exalted: «افترى على الله كذبا أم به جنة», because informing while in a state of madness is other than lying, since it is set against it as a separate category, and other than truth, since they believed he was not truthful; thus the intermediate category is established. This was refuted on the grounds that the meaning is "or has he not fabricated", and the absence of fabrication was expressed by madness inasmuch as a madman has no fabrication, because fabrication is deliberate lying. So this is a restriction of the false statement, by their claim, into its two kinds, i.e. lying deliberately and not deliberately.
* Vocabulary:
(اسْتَحْوَذَ): he took control and prevailed; from حاذ الحمار العانة, i.e. the wild ass gathered the herd and drove it, prevailing over it; and from it: "he was an أحوذي, unique of his kind". It is one of the words that came according to the original form, like استصوب and استنوق, i.e. contrary to the analogical rule, for the analogical form would be استحاذ, with the wāw turned into alif, as in استعاذ and استقام; but استحوذ here is better.
(يُحَادُّونَ): they oppose.

dervis-irab:18-22.t:
* I'rab:
(يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعاً فَيَحْلِفُونَ لَهُ كَما يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ): يوم is accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember), and the clause is resumptive; the clause يبعثهم is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; الله is the fāʿil (agent) of يبعثهم; جميعا is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the fāʿ is conjunctive; يحلفون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; له is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يحلفون; كما is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); the clause يحلفون has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative [ما]; and لكم is attached to يحلفون.
(وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ عَلى شَيْءٍ أَلا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْكاذِبُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial, and the clause يحسبون is a ḥāl from the wāw in يحلفون له, i.e. while they think in the Hereafter that their swearing there will benefit them against its punishment. أنّ and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) filling the place of the two objects of يحسبون; على شيء is the khabar (predicate) of أنهم. ألا is a particle of opening and alerting; إنّ with its noun; هم is an attached pronoun [Translator's note: so in the source; the parallel passages below say "a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl)", which is presumably what is meant] or a mubtadaʾ (subject); الكاذبون is the khabar of إنهم on the first view, and its [هم's] khabar on the second, the clause then being the khabar of إنهم.
(اسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّيْطانُ فَأَنْساهُمْ ذِكْرَ اللَّهِ): a resumptive statement brought to explain Satan's control over them, to the point that he made them his followers and his flock. عليهم is attached to استحوذ and الشيطان is its fāʿil; فأنساهم is conjoined to استحوذ, the hāʾ being the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and ذكر الله the second mafʿūl bihi.
(أُولئِكَ حِزْبُ الشَّيْطانِ أَلا إِنَّ حِزْبَ الشَّيْطانِ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and حزب الشيطان the khabar; ألا is a particle of opening and alerting; إنّ with its noun; هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; and الخاسرون is the khabar in both cases, as has preceded.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحَادُّونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ أُولئِكَ فِي الْأَذَلِّينَ): إنّ and its noun; the clause يحادون is the ṣila; الله is the mafʿūl bihi and رسوله is conjoined to الله; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and في الأذلين is the khabar of أولئك, and the clause is the khabar of إنّ.
(كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَأَغْلِبَنَّ أَنَا وَرُسُلِي إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ): كتب الله is a verb and its fāʿil; the verb كتب carries the meaning of an oath, and the lām is its answer; أغلبنّ is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its connection with the heavy nūn of emphasis; أنا is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent fāʿil of أغلبنّ; رسلي is conjoined to the pronoun; and إنّ with its noun and its two predicates; and the clauses have no grammatical position.
(لا تَجِدُ قَوْماً يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ يُوادُّونَ مَنْ حَادَّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ): Al-Zamakhsharī said: «This is of the category of imaginative representation (takhyīl): it is represented that it is impossible and absurd that you should find a people who are believers taking the idolaters as allies; and the purpose of this is that this ought not to be, and its due is that it be impossible and not exist in any circumstance, by way of exaggeration in forbidding it and deterring from involvement in it, and enjoining firmness in avoiding the enemies of Allah and keeping far from them, and guarding against mixing and associating with them.» لا is negating; تجد is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "أنت"; قوما is the first mafʿūl bihi; the clause يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر is a naʿt (adjective) of قوما; the clause يوادّون is the second object of تجد if it means "know", and if it means "come upon", the clause is a ḥāl or a second adjective of قوما. يوادّون is a verb and its fāʿil; من is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause حاد الله is the ṣila, with no grammatical position; حاد الله is a past verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; and رسوله is conjoined to الله.
(وَلَوْ كانُوا آباءَهُمْ أَوْ أَبْناءَهُمْ أَوْ إِخْوانَهُمْ أَوْ عَشِيرَتَهُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial; لو is conditional; كان with its noun, and آباءهم is its predicate, what follows being conjoined to it. The secret of the ordering will come in the section on rhetoric.
(أُولئِكَ كَتَبَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْإِيمانَ وَأَيَّدَهُمْ بِرُوحٍ مِنْهُ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and the clause كتب is the khabar; في قلوبهم is attached to كتب; الإيمان is the mafʿūl bihi; أيدهم is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; بروح is attached to أيدهم; and منه is an adjective of روح.
(وَيُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها): the wāw is conjunctive; يدخلهم is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; جنات is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause تجري من تحتها الأنهار is an adjective of جنات; خالدين is a ḥāl; and فيها is attached to خالدين.
(رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ أُولئِكَ حِزْبُ اللَّهِ أَلا إِنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ): رضي is a past verb and الله its fāʿil; عنهم is attached to رضي; ورضوا عنه is conjoined to what precedes. أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and حزب الله the khabar; ألا is a particle of opening and alerting; إنّ with its noun; هم is a pronoun of separation or a mubtadaʾ; and المفلحون is the khabar. The like of this has preceded many times.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ولو كانوا آباءهم أو أبناءهم أو إخوانهم أو عشيرتهم» a wonderful ordering has been observed. He began first with the fathers, because they most call for concern for them, owing to the obligation of sincere obedience to them; and despite that, He forbade them from loving them. Allah the Exalted said:
«وإن جاهداك لتشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما وصاحبهما في الدنيا معروفا». Secondly He mentioned the sons, because they cling most closely to the core of the heart; then thirdly the brothers, because they are the refuge in time of need and the helper when crises break out, as it has been said:
أخاك أخاك إن من لا أخا له ... كساع إلى الهيجا بغير سلاح
(Your brother, your brother! For whoever has no brother is like one running into battle without a weapon.)
Then fourthly the kinsfolk, because they are the ones whose help is sought in hardships; they are the refuge and the resort in calamities, and they are the ones who hasten to give aid. [The poet] said:
لا يسألون أخاهم حين يندبهم ... في النائبات على ما قال برهانا
(They do not ask their brother, when he calls on them in calamities, for proof of what he says.)
Those intended in the verse are Abū ʿUbayda, because he killed his father on the day of Uḥud; Abū Bakr, because he challenged his son to single combat on the day of Badr, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered him to sit back; Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr, because he killed his brother Abū ʿAzīz on the day of Uḥud; and ʿAlī and others who killed members of their clans.

dervis-irab:1-4.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَظْهَرُونَ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads «يُظاهِرُونَ»]: the imperfect of «ظاهر». It was also read «يظّهّرون» with doubling of the ẓāʾ and the hāʾ; and «يتظاهرون», the imperfect of «تظاهر», and «يتظهّرون», the imperfect of «تظهّر». What is meant by all of it is ẓihār, which is a man's saying to his wife "You are to me like my mother's back", meaning with respect to prohibition — as though it alluded to riding, since that is known on the backs of animals — and the meaning is that he does not mount her, just as he does not mount his mother. In al-Qāmūs: "Ẓihār is his saying to his wife 'You are to me like my mother's back'; and «ظاهر منها», «تظهّر» and «ظهّر» [are said]." More discussion of this root will come in the Benefits section.

* I'rab:
(قَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّتِي تُجادِلُكَ فِي زَوْجِها وَتَشْتَكِي إِلَى اللَّهِ): «قد» is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); «سمع الله» is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent) — al-Kisāʾī assimilated the dāl into the sīn; «قول» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «التي» is a relative noun in the position of genitive by annexation; the clause «تجادلك» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. «تجادلك» is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring to the woman mentioned — her story will come in the Benefits section — and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi. (For this reason the surah was named al-Mujādila, with kasra on the dāl, as an active participle; it was also said with fatḥa and with kasra, as in the gloss of al-Shihāb on al-Bayḍāwī; the kasra is preferable in any case because it is more suited to the context.) «في زوجها» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تجادلك», and a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "concerning the affair of her husband". «تشتكي» is conjoined to «تجادلك»; it is also permissible that the wāw be circumstantial and the clause in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). «إلى الله» is attached to «تشتكي».
(وَاللَّهُ يَسْمَعُ تَحاوُرَكُما إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ): the wāw is circumstantial; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause «يسمع» the khabar (predicate); the fāʿil is latent, referring to Allah; «تحاوركما» is the mafʿūl bihi. Ḥiwār in speech is well known. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«حاورته» means I exchanged speech with him; «تحاورا» [they conversed]; and «أحار الرجل الجواب», with alif, means he returned it; and «ما أحاره» means he did not return it." [Then] «إنّ» and its noun and its two predicates, and the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya) for what precedes it.
(الَّذِينَ يُظاهِرُونَ مِنْكُمْ مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ ما هُنَّ أُمَّهاتِهِمْ): resumptive speech, set forth to begin explaining the rulings on the one who makes ẓihār. «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ; the clause «يظاهرون» is the ṣila and has no grammatical position; «منكم» is a ḥāl, i.e. in the state of their being from among you, O Arabs; and what is in this ḥāl of disparagement of their customs and rebuke of them is not hidden. «من نسائهم» is attached to «يظاهرون», i.e. they forbid their wives to themselves like Allah's forbidding to them the backs of their mothers. «ما» is the Ḥijāzī negating «ما» [which operates like «ليس»]; «هنّ» is its noun and «أمهاتهم» its khabar, made accusative with the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, which is the relative noun.
(إِنْ أُمَّهاتُهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّائِي وَلَدْنَهُمْ): «إن» is negating; «أمهاتهم» is a mubtadaʾ; «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «اللائي» is a relative noun in the position of nominative as khabar; the clause «ولدنهم» is the ṣila; «ولدنهم» is a verb, its fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi.
(وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَقُولُونَ مُنْكَراً مِنَ الْقَوْلِ وَزُوراً): the wāw is a conjunction; «إنهم» is «إنّ» and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «يقولون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of «إنهم»; «منكرا» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a reprehensible saying"; «زورا» is conjoined to «منكرا».
(وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «إنّ» and its noun, and the shifted lām; «عفوّ» is a first khabar and «غفور» a second khabar.
(وَالَّذِينَ يُظاهِرُونَ مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِما قالُوا فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَتَمَاسَّا): resumptive speech, set forth to detail the ruling on ẓihār after explaining that it is reprehensible; you may also conjoin the speech to what preceded so that the ruling is arranged in a primary arrangement. «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ; the clause «يظاهرون» is the ṣila; «من نسائهم» is attached to «يظاهرون». «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay; «يعودون» is conjoined to «يظاهرون». «لما»: the lām is a preposition and «ما» is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يعودون», i.e. they return to their saying. You may also make «ما» a relative noun with the clause as its ṣila and the referring pronoun omitted, i.e. "to what they said". The fāʾ links [the predicate] because of the meaning of condition in the relative noun; «تحرير رقبة» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "upon him is the freeing of a slave", and the clause is the khabar of «الذين». «من قبل» is attached to an omitted ḥāl; «أن» with what follows it is interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of genitive by annexation.
(ذلِكُمْ تُوعَظُونَ بِهِ وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ): «ذلكم» is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the ruling mentioned; the clause «توعظون» is the khabar — for penalties are deterrents from committing crimes. «الله» is a mubtadaʾ; «بما» is attached to «خبير»; the clause «تعملون» is the ṣila; «خبير» is the khabar of «الله».
(فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتابِعَيْنِ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَتَمَاسَّا): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «من» is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ; «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; «يجد» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لم», and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "هو". «فصيام»: the fāʾ is linking and «صيام» is a mubtadaʾ; «شهرين» is muḍāf ilayhi and «متتابعين» an adjective; the khabar is omitted, i.e. "upon him", and the clause is the khabar of «من». The i'rab of «من قبل أن يتماسا» has preceded.
(فَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَإِطْعامُ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِيناً): its i'rab has preceded; «مسكينا» is a tamyīz (specification).
(ذلِكَ لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ): «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the foregoing explanation and teaching; «لتؤمنوا»: the lām of causation, and what it enters upon is the khabar of «ذلك». It is also permissible to parse the demonstrative as accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "We did that so that you may believe". «بالله» is attached to «تؤمنوا»; «رسوله» is conjoined to «الله».
(وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ وَلِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «تلك» is a mubtadaʾ and «حدود الله» the khabar; the wāw is a conjunction; «للكافرين» is a fronted khabar and «عذاب» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «أليم» is an adjective of «عذاب».

* Rhetoric:
In the verse of ẓihār there is a wonderful device among the devices of rhetoric, namely negation and affirmation (al-salb wa-l-ījāb). Reference to it has preceded: it is building the speech on denying a thing from one aspect and affirming it from another aspect, or commanding a thing from one aspect and forbidding it from a second aspect. In His saying «الذين يظاهرون منكم من نسائهم ما هن أمهاتهم إن أمهاتهم إلا اللائي ولدنهم» there is a denial that the wife becomes a mother through ẓihār, and an affirmation of motherhood for the one who gave birth to the child.

* Benefits:
He said in al-Kashshāf: "ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: 'Praise be to Allah whose hearing encompasses all voices. The woman who disputed spoke to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a corner of the house while I was with him, and I could not hear, yet He heard her.' And it is reported from ʿUmar that when she came in to him he would honour her and say: 'Allah has heard her.'" As for the woman, she is Khawla bint Thaʿlaba, the wife of Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit, her paternal cousin. He saw her praying — she was comely and of beautiful body — and when she finished with the salām he sought intercourse with her, but she refused. He became angry — he had a touch of madness — and said: "You are to me like my mother's back." She came to the Messenger of Allah and complained to him of her affair. It is reported that she said to him: "I have small children; if I leave them with him they will be lost, and if I keep them with me they will go hungry." He said: "I have nothing concerning your affair." It is also reported that he said to her: "I do not see you except that you have become forbidden to him, and I have not been commanded anything regarding you." She said: "I complain to Allah of my poverty and my grief." So these verses were revealed. The rulings on ẓihār and the schools of the imams concerning it are set out at length in the books of jurisprudence, so refer to them if you wish.

dervis-irab:5-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُحَادُّونَ): they show enmity and opposition. The wording of al-Zajjāj: muḥādda is that you are on a boundary (ḥadd) different from your companion's boundary; so muḥādda is a metonymy (kināya) for enmity, since it is a necessary concomitant of enmity. In the lexicons: "«حادّه» means he was hostile to him and angered him."
(كُبِتُوا): they were seized and destroyed; it was also said: they were humiliated. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«كبت الله العدو كبتا», of the pattern «ضرب», means He disgraced him and humiliated him; and «كبته لوجهه» means he threw him down on his face."

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحَادُّونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ كُبِتُوا كَما كُبِتَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): resumptive speech, set forth to convey good tidings to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the believers of the subduing of their enemies, their humiliation, the breaking of their bonds and the splitting of their unity. «إنّ» and its noun; the clause «يحادون» is the ṣila (relative clause); «الله» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and «رسوله» is conjoined to «الله»; the clause «كبتوا» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ». «كما» is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); the clause «كبت» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the particle-relative [i.e. the maṣdar-forming «ما»]; «الذين» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); «من قبلهم» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element that is the ṣila of «الذين».
(وَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنا آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ وَلِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ): the wāw is circumstantial; «قد» is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); «أنزلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «آيات» is the mafʿūl bihi and «بيّنات» an adjective of «آيات»; «للكافرين» is a fronted khabar and «عذاب» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); «مهين» is an adjective.
(يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعاً فَيُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِما عَمِلُوا أَحْصاهُ اللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُ): the adverb may be attached to «مهين»; it was also said that its governor is «عذاب»; it was said that its governor is the settling (istiqrār) to which the khabar, namely «للكافرين», is attached; and it was said that it is accusative by an implied "remember". The clause «يبعثهم» is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; «الله» is the fāʿil of «يبعثهم»; «جميعا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). «فينبئهم» is conjoined to «يبعثهم»; «بما عملوا» is in the position of the second object; the clause «عملوا» is the ṣila of the relative noun. The clause «أحصاه الله» is resumptive; the wāw is circumstantial, and the clause «نسوه» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the object of «أحصى», with an implied «قد» or without it.
(وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ): «الله» is a mubtadaʾ; «على كل شيء» is attached to «شهيد»; «شهيد» is the khabar of «الله».
(أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr); «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; «تر» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter. «أنّ» and its noun, and the clause «يعلم» is its khabar, and it stands in place of the two objects of «تر». «ما» is the object of «يعلم»; «في السموات» is attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila of the relative noun; «ما في الأرض» is conjoined to «ما في السموات».
(ما يَكُونُ مِنْ نَجْوى ثَلاثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رابِعُهُمْ وَلا خَمْسَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ سادِسُهُمْ): resumptive speech, set forth to affirm the vastness of His knowledge, the Exalted, and to explain its manner. «ما» is negating; «يكون» is a complete (tāmm) imperfect verb; «من» is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and «نجوى» is genitive by «من» in form and the fāʿil of «يكون» in position; «ثلاثة» is annexed to «نجوى» [as muḍāf ilayhi]. «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «رابعهم» the khabar; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, so the exception is "emptied" (mufarragh) from the most general of states. «ولا خمسة إلا هو سادسهم» is conjoined to what preceded.
(وَلا أَدْنى مِنْ ذلِكَ وَلا أَكْثَرَ إِلَّا هُوَ مَعَهُمْ أَيْنَ ما كانُوا): the wāw is a conjunction; «لا» is negating; «أدنى» is conjoined to the form of «نجوى». It was also read in the nominative, conjoined to its position, and it was said: as a mubtadaʾ. «من ذلك» is attached to «أدنى»; «ولا أكثر» is conjoined to «ولا أدنى». «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ; «معهم» is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar; the clause is circumstantial on the accusative reading or [the reading of] conjunction to the position, and a khabar of the mubtadaʾ on the nominative reading. «أينما» is an adverb of place attached to the settling to which «معهم» is attached, i.e. accompanying them with His knowledge in whatever place they settle. «كانوا» is a verb and its fāʿil, so it is the complete «كان», and the clause is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it, because «ما» was added in it. It is also permissible that «ما» be maṣdar-forming, so that the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the particle-relative.
(ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِما عَمِلُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ): «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence; «ينبئهم» is an imperfect verb, with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil referring to Allah; «بما» is in the position of the second object; the clause «عملوا» has no grammatical position; «يوم القيامة» is attached to «ينبئهم»; [then] «إنّ» and its noun and its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثة إلا هو رابعهم ولا خمسة إلا هو سادسهم ولا أدنى من ذلك ولا أكثر إلا هو معهم» there is the device of al-infiṣāl (extrication). Reference to it has preceded, and we repeat it here to complete the benefit. We say: it is a device whose gist is that the speaker says something against which an objection can be raised, and he does not stop at it until he brings what extricates him from that, either overtly or covertly, in a way that interpretation brings out. For against the apparent sense of this noble verse a number of questions can be raised, among them:
1- Why was beginning with two omitted in it, when that is the first rank among those who converse in secret?
2- Why did He move from three to five, departing from the order of moving from three to four?
3- Why did He not go beyond five as He went beyond three?
4- Why did He not say «من نجوى ثلاثة» and stop at that, making do with His saying after it «ولا أدنى من ذلك ولا أكثر», so that the lesser would cover two and the greater would cover four up to the endless numbers?
5- Why did He turn from the more concise to the longer, although the more concise fully conveys the intended meaning?
Before we explain the extrication from this, a historical glimpse must be mentioned, by which the veil is lifted. There is disagreement about the occasion of its revelation. It was said: the idolaters gathered in groups of these two numbers, three by three and five by five, conversing secretly about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, thinking that this was hidden from him; so it was revealed so that Allah would inform His Prophet of their state. It was also said: three men of Quraysh gathered one day — Rabīʿa and Ḥabīb, the two sons of ʿAmr, and Ṣafwān ibn Umayya — and were talking. One of them said: "Do you think Allah knows what we say?" Another said: "He knows some and does not know some." The third said: "If He knows some, then He knows all." So it was revealed. The exegetes have authenticated this second report.
Al-Zamakhsharī said, in answer to some of the objections to the apparent sense of the verse mentioned above, after quoting the occasion of revelation that we have mentioned: that the Creator, Mighty and Majestic — and He knows best — intended to mention the customary numbers of the people of secret conversation and the people of consultation; those delegated for that are not all the people, but only a select group of people of intellect and forbearance, and a band of people of experience and judgement; their number starts at two and goes up to six, as the situation requires and as sound judgement decides. Do you not see that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, left the consultation (shūrā) among six and did not go beyond them to a seventh? [Translator's note: what follows is the author's quotation of another critic (the wording matches Ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ in Taḥrīr al-Taḥbīr / Badīʿ al-Qurʾān); the source does not name him here.] This is the text of al-Zamakhsharī's words; I have reported it in his wording, leaving nothing out of it and not replacing a word with a word. As for the first report he related, there is no difficulty in it and no objection against it. As for the second report, which was authenticated — it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him — the difficulty applies to it. As for al-Zamakhsharī's saying that the speech came according to the custom of the Arabs regarding the people of secret conversation and the people of consultation, because the number of these two groups does not exceed six; and as for his citing as evidence the case of ʿUmar and his putting the consultation among six, and his emphasising that by his saying "Do you not see that he did not go beyond six with the meaning of consultation to a seventh?" — I do not know where he got that from! How can his claim be valid that, in the custom of the Arabs, the people of secret conversation and the people of consultation are only of these two numbers and not other numbers, when the Mighty Quran has come with the opposite of that? Allah the Exalted said, informing about the sons of Yaʿqūb: «فلما استيأسوا منه خلصوا نجيا», and they were ten; so He, glorified is He, called their conversation secret conversing. And He, Mighty and Majestic, said, relating about the chiefs of Pharaoh: «وأسروا النجوى» «إن هذان لساحران», and they could not be counted for their multitude. And the Exalted said: «يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ناجيتم الرسول فقدموا بين يدي نجواكم صدقة»; and those who converse privately with the Messenger could be two and upward to the full number of the Community, for the address is to all the believers, and He, glorified is He, did not restrict the number of those conversing to a definite amount. And He, glorified is He, said: «فلا تتناجوا بالإثم والعدوان ومعصية الرسول», not restricting that to a fixed number; and He, glorified is He, said: «وأمرهم شورى بينهم», with no definite number. Even though some of these verses were revealed about a specific incident, Allah sent down their meaning in general wording so as to include the whole Community, so the ruling in them is general. As for the case of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, it is known that he did not put the matter to consultation among those six out of regard for this number; he only had regard for those fit for the matter. The six among whom he placed the matter were the notables of the Companions and the best of those who remained after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and after the two shaykhs (Abū Bakr and ʿUmar), and the matter was not permitted to go outside them or pass beyond them to others. Had those fit for this matter been more than this number or fewer, he would have placed the matter among them, and would not have cared whether they fell short of this number or exceeded it.
What is fit to be an answer, by which one is extricated from the difficulty set out at the beginning of the discussion, is to say: those about whom the revelation of the verse is authentically reported are the three whom Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, named. Since this number, I mean three, is what is intended by the verse, it was mentioned first in it, before the last number, so that His concern with it would be known [Translator's note: the source has «ليعلم أئمتهم به», apparently a corruption of «ليُعلَم اهتمامه به»], for when the speaker has concern for something, he mentions it in his speech before other things in matters like these. Then He mentioned the lesser and the greater to remove the possibility that we presented earlier. If this is the incident because of which the verse was revealed, the first question falls away, in which it was said: why did He not mention the first rank of those who converse secretly, and make do with mentioning "the lesser" after mentioning three so as to cover two, or "the greater" to cover what is above three?
The answer to the saying "What is the benefit of mentioning five after mentioning three, when the saying of the Exalted «ولا أكثر» makes it and others up to the endless unnecessary?" is that He, glorified is He, wanted to teach us the manner of moving through these numbers, rising from three to five, so that it would be known that the reference is to all the ranks of numbers, and that the manner of moving in the rest is like the manner [of moving] to five. If it is said: "Then why was this teaching not by four, which was omitted? Mentioning it would have been more fitting, because moving from three to four is more correct than moving from three to five, for numbers coming in order is more correct than their coming out of order, and the purpose of teaching the manner of moving would have been achieved by that," I say: two things prevented that. One of them is the fear that the composition of the speech would come out faulty, because of its heaviness on the tongue and the ear, due to the ugliness of repeating the word for four with no barrier keeping one of the two words apart from the other. For if it were said «إلا هو رابعهم ولا أربعة», the speech would be heavy because of the adjacency of two words in which there are four letters of the throat, namely the two ʿayns and the two hāʾs. Al-Āmidī faulted Abū Tammām for the like of this in his saying:
كريم متى أمدحه أمدحه والورى ... معي وإذا ما لمته لمته وحدي
(A noble man: whenever I praise him, I praise him with all mankind joining me; and whenever I blame him, I blame him alone.)
and he called it muʿāẓala (entanglement), which is the most hideous of the faults that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb denied of the poetry of Zuhayr when he characterised it — although someone other than al-Āmidī counted muʿāẓala as something other than this. The second thing that prevented mentioning four is the eloquent composer's fleeing from repeating meanings and words without benefit. Had He moved to four, the ruling would have been repeated, because the ruling on it has already been given in five, for five is four and more, so four is included in it, and whatever rulings apply to it apply to four. Also, [there is] fleeing from mentioning the even and turning from it to mentioning the odd, because of the merits that make the odd deserve mention rather than the even, which others do not have. In this answer given to the second question there is an answer to the third question. As for the answer to the fourth question, namely his saying: "Why did He not move from five to seven as He moved from three to five and end at that limit, instead of neglecting this number which is distinguished by properties Allah the Exalted placed in it, because of which the number of the heavens and the earth, the days of time, the climes of the earth, and things there is no room to mention came in accordance with it?" — we say: the intention was to teach the manner of moving, and that was achieved by mentioning five; so repeating it with another number is a useless lengthening made unnecessary by what preceded it. If the properties of seven were regarded, it would be necessary to regard the properties of nine as well. The intention of the verse is not to draw attention to the properties of numbers; the intention is only what we have mentioned. Otherwise, whenever the properties of numbers are considered, you will find five distinguished by what no other number is distinguished by. Among its properties in which it is unique is that it is the first number that gathers three odd numbers: one, three and five; and among them is that the number of its odd numbers is odd, and this does not belong to any other among all the numbers of the rank of units, nor to what is built on its basis and branches from it. For three gathers only two odd numbers, and the number of its odd numbers is likewise even. As for seven, even though it gathers four odd numbers, the number of its odd numbers is even, and it is compound in relation to five, because it is five and more, while five is simple in relation to it, and the simple is the root of the compound. Nine, even though it gathers more than seven and the number of its odd numbers comes out odd, is compound in relation to seven, which is compound in relation to five; so five, in relation to it, is the root of the root. Since five has this standing, mentioning it was more fitting than mentioning seven, and it had to be brought in order to draw attention to the honour and excellence it has over others, and one must stop at it and limit the teaching of the manner of moving to it. By this it is established that the composition of the verse as it came is more eloquent than what the one raising the question and the one singling out the difficulty imagined.
Al-Karkhī said: "He singled out three and five for mention because a group of the hypocrites stayed behind to converse secretly, and they were of the number mentioned, to vex the believers; so the verse was revealed with a description of their state and as a making known of them. Or because the odd number is nobler than the even, since Allah the Exalted is odd (witr) and loves the odd; so the two numbers mentioned were singled out for mention to draw attention to the fact that divine matters must be observed in all matters. Then after mentioning them, what is added to them covers others among those who converse secretly."
Al-Khāzin has a fine passage that we quote as follows to complete the discussion. He said: "If you say: why did He single out three and five? I say: because the least that suffices in consultation is three, so that the purpose is achieved: two are like disputants over the negative and the affirmative, and the third is like the mediator judging between them; then consultation is praiseworthy and the purpose is achieved. Likewise every group that gathers for consultation must have one who is an arbiter among them whose word is accepted. It was also said that the odd number is nobler than the even; for this reason Allah the Exalted singled out three and five."

dervis-irab:8-10.t:
* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ نُهُوا عَنِ النَّجْوى ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِما نُهُوا عَنْهُ): resumptive speech, set forth to explain another pattern of their secret conversation and their winking among themselves — they being the Jews and the hypocrites — whenever they saw the believers, intending by that to provoke them and inflame their anger. The Prophet ﷺ often forbade them from that, but they would hardly desist before returning to the like of what they had done. The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr); «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; «تر» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت"; «إلى الذين» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تر». The clause «نهوا» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; «نهوا» is a passive past verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); «عن النجوى» is attached to «نهوا». «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay; «يعودون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). He turned away from the past form suited to the conjunction for a subtle secret, namely calling to mind the image of the returning, its renewal and its embodiment. «لما» is attached to «يعودون»; the clause «نهوا» is the ṣila; «عنه» is attached to «نهوا».
(وَيَتَناجَوْنَ بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوانِ وَمَعْصِيَةِ الرَّسُولِ): the wāw is a conjunction; «يتناجون» is an imperfect verb conjoined to «يعودون» — and in the imperfect form there is what was just mentioned of embodiment, calling to mind and renewal. «بالإثم» is attached to «يتناجون»; «العدوان» is conjoined to «الإثم», and «معصية الرسول» is also conjoined.
(وَإِذا جاؤُكَ حَيَّوْكَ بِما لَمْ يُحَيِّكَ بِهِ اللَّهُ): the wāw is a conjunction; «إذا» is an adverb for future time; the clause «جاءوك» is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; the wāw is the fāʿil and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «حيّوك» has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition; «بما» is attached to «حيّوك», i.e. they addressed you. «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; «يحيك» is an imperfect verb made jussive by «لم», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi and «الله» the fāʿil; i.e. with what Allah did not legislate or permit. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«حيّاه تحية»: its origin is praying for life; from it is «التحيات لله», i.e. permanence — it was also said: dominion. Then it became frequent until it was used for prayer in general; then the Law used it for a specific prayer, namely «سلام عليك»."
(وَيَقُولُونَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ لَوْلا يُعَذِّبُنَا اللَّهُ بِما نَقُولُ): the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; «يقولون» is an imperfect verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; «في أنفسهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), i.e. "هلّا"; «يعذبنا الله» is an imperfect verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi and a postponed fāʿil; «بما» is attached to «يعذبنا», and «ما» is maṣdar-forming, i.e. "for our saying"; it may also be a relative noun with the referring pronoun omitted, i.e. "for what we say". The clause is the speech quoted (maqūl al-qawl).
(حَسْبُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ يَصْلَوْنَها فَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ): «حسبهم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «جهنم» the khabar (predicate); the clause «يصلونها» is a ḥāl. The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); «بئس» is a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; «المصير» is the fāʿil; the one specified for blame is omitted, i.e. "it".
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا تَناجَيْتُمْ فَلا تَتَناجَوْا بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوانِ وَمَعْصِيَةِ الرَّسُولِ): «إذا» is an adverb for future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause «تناجيتم» is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; the fāʾ links the answer of «إذا»; «لا» is prohibitive; «تتناجوا» is an imperfect verb made jussive by «لا», and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition. «بالإثم» is attached to «تتناجوا»; «العدوان» is conjoined to His saying «بالإثم», and «معصية الرسول» is also conjoined.
(وَتَناجَوْا بِالْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوى وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; «تناجوا» is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; «بالبرّ» is attached to «تناجوا»; «التقوى» is conjoined to «البرّ». «اتقوا الله» is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi; «الذي» is an adjective of «الله»; «إليه» is attached to «تحشرون»; «تحشرون» is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun.
(إِنَّمَا النَّجْوى مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ لِيَحْزُنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): «إنما» is a restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa); «النجوى» is a mubtadaʾ and «من الشيطان» the khabar. The lām is the lām of causation; «يحزن» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām; the lām with its genitive noun is a second khabar. One says «حزنه» and «أحزنه» with the same meaning. «الذين» is the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila. It was also said that the relative noun is the fāʿil of «يحزن».
(وَلَيْسَ بِضارِّهِمْ شَيْئاً إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): the wāw is circumstantial; «ليس» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent, its implied form being "هو"; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and «ضارّهم» is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of «ليس»; «شيئا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. something of harm; «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «بإذن الله» is attached to «ضارّهم».
(وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and «على الله» is attached to «يتوكل».

dervis-irab:11-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَفَسَّحُوا): make room and do not crowd one another. In al-Asās: "«افسحوا لأخيكم في المجلس وتفسحوا له» (make room for your brother in the gathering); and «ما لك في هذا المكان منفسح» (you have no room in this place)."
(انْشُزُوا): rise up to make room for those arriving. In al-Asās about it: "«علوت نشزا من الأرض ونشزا وأنشازا» (I climbed a raised piece of ground); «نشز الشيء» means it rose; «نشز عن مكانه» means he rose and stood up from his place; «وإذا قيل انشزوا فانشزوا»; and «أنشزه» means he raised it from its place." The nūn followed by the shīn, as first and second radicals, has a special, wonderful property, namely indicating speed and rising. One says: «أنشأ الله الخلق فنشئوا» (Allah brought the creation into being and they grew up); «أنشأ قصيدة وشعرا وعمارة» (he composed an ode, poetry; he put up a building); «أنشأ يفعل كذا» (he set about doing such-and-such); «من أين نشأت» and «أنشأت», i.e. where did you rise up from. «نشب العظم في الحلق» (the bone stuck in the throat), «[نشب] الصيد في الحبالة» (the game got caught in the snare), «[نشبت] مخالب الجارح في الأخيذة» (the talons of the bird of prey sank into the prey); «تنشّب» and «أنشب فيه مخالبه» (he sank his talons into it); «رماه بنشّابة» (he shot him with an arrow) and «تراموا بالنّشّاب والنشاشيب» (they shot arrows at one another). In all of that the meaning of speed appears clearly. «نشب الشر والحرب بينهم نشوبا» (evil and war broke out between them); «لم ينشب أن قال», in the sense of "he did not delay [before saying]". «نشج الباكي نشيجا» — this is choking with weeping, its rising and its resounding in the chest. «أنشدني شعرا إنشادا حسنا» (he recited poetry to me well), because the reciter raises his voice with what he recites. «نشر الثوب والكتاب» (he spread out the garment and the book) [Translator's note: the source has «الثواب», evidently for «الثوب»], «نشّر الثياب والكتب», «صحف منشّرة» (scrolls spread out), «ملاء منشّر» (spread-out sheets); «نشر الله الموتى نشرا» (Allah resurrected the dead); «له نشر طيب», which is what spreads and rises of its scent. Al-Muraqqish said, describing women:
النشر مسك والوجوه دنا ... نير وأطراف الأكفّ عنم
(Their scent is musk, their faces are dinars, and their fingertips are ʿanam [a red plant].)
«نشّ اللحم في المقلاة نشيشا» (the meat sizzled in the pan) [Translator's note: the source has «نشيئا»], and wine «تنش» when it begins to bubble. «رجل نشيط»: a man eager and willing for work, quick in it. «نشع الصبي الدواء وأنشعه» means he poured the medicine into the child's mouth, «فانتشعه» (and he took it in) — and speed is noted in it; «إنه لمنشوع بأكل اللحم» when he is passionately fond of it. «نشف الماء بنفسه» (the water dried up of itself): it was quick to dry up. «نشق الظبي في الحبالة» (the gazelle got stuck in the snare): it was caught in it — the meaning of this has passed. «استنشقت الريح وتنشّقتها» (I inhaled the wind). Al-Mutalammis said:
فلو أن محموما بخيبر مدنفا ... تنشّق رياها لأقلع صالبه
(If a man sick with fever in Khaybar, gravely ill, were to inhale her fragrance, his fever would leave him.)
«نشل اللحم من القدر بالمنشل والمنشال» (he snatched the meat out of the pot with the minshal or minshāl), which is a piece of iron with a hook at its head. «نشّم اللحم» means corruption came quickly to the meat and it began to smell. ʿAlqama said:
وقد أصاحب فتيانا طعامهم ... خضر المزاد ولحم فيه تنشيم
(I have kept company with young men whose food is the green water of water-skins and meat that has begun to spoil.)
i.e. they are given algae-covered water and smelly meat to eat; he used a predominating term (taghlīb) and said "their food". «نشّموا في الشر» (they plunged into evil) and «دقوا بينهم عطر منشم» (they pounded the perfume of Manshim between them). Zuhayr said:
تداركتما عبسا وذبيان بعد ما ... تفانوا ودقّوا بينهم عطر منشم
(You two rescued ʿAbs and Dhubyān after they had all but annihilated each other and pounded the perfume of Manshim between them.)
«رجل نشوان» (a tipsy man), whom intoxication reached quickly; «امرأة نشوى» and «قوم نشاوى». «نشيت منه رائحة طيبة» (I smelled a pleasant scent from him) and «استنشيت». This is among the wonders by which languages are distinguished.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا قِيلَ لَكُمْ تَفَسَّحُوا فِي الْمَجالِسِ فَافْسَحُوا يَفْسَحِ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ): «إذا» is an adverb for future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause «قيل» is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; «لكم» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قيل». «تفسحوا» is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause «تفسحوا» is the speech quoted (maqūl al-qawl); «في المجالس» is attached to «تفسحوا». The fāʾ links the answer of the non-jussive condition, and the clause has no grammatical position; «افسحوا» is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; «يفسح» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the command that occurs as the answer of the condition; «الله» is the fāʿil; «لكم» is attached to «يفسح». What is meant by the gatherings is the gatherings of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It was also read in the singular, i.e. «في المجلس». It was also said that it is the station among the stations of fighting and the posts of the warriors; and it was said that it is unrestricted, covering everything people seek for benefit, and every gathering or assembly — this is preferable and nearest to the style of the Noble Quran in teaching lofty manners.
(وَإِذا قِيلَ انْشُزُوا فَانْشُزُوا يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجاتٍ): the wāw is a conjunction. «وإذا قيل انشزوا فانشزوا»: the i'rab of its counterpart has preceded. «يرفع» is an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the answer to the request; «الله» is the fāʿil; «الذين» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause). «الذين» is conjoined to the first «الذين», or it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "and He singles out those who were given knowledge". The clause «أوتوا» is the ṣila; «أوتوا» is a passive past verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); «العلم» is the second mafʿūl bihi; «منكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «درجات» is an adverb, or accusative by removal of the preposition.
(وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ): the wāw is resumptive; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «بما تعملون» is attached to «خبير»; «خبير» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ» [Translator's note: so in the source; there is no «إنّ» here, and «خبير» is the khabar of «الله»].
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا ناجَيْتُمُ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ نَجْواكُمْ صَدَقَةً): «إذا» is a future adverb containing the meaning of condition; the clause «ناجيتم» is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; «ناجيتم» is a verb and its fāʿil, and «الرسول» is the mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ is linking; «قدّموا» is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition. «بين» is an adverb attached to «قدّموا»; «يدي» is muḍāf ilayhi, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ; «نجواكم» is annexed to «يدي»; «صدقة» is the mafʿūl bihi of «قدّموا». Further discussion of this verse will come in the Rhetoric section.
(ذلِكَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَأَطْهَرُ): «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to giving charity before the private conversation; «خير» is the khabar; «لكم» is attached to «خير»; «أطهر» is conjoined to «خير».
(فَإِنْ لَمْ تَجِدُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «إن» is conditional; «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; «تجدوا» is an imperfect verb made jussive by «لم», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). The fāʾ links an omitted apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), i.e. "then there is no blame on you"; the clause «إن الله غفور رحيم» is the reason for the removal of hardship and blame.
(أَأَشْفَقْتُمْ أَنْ تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ نَجْواكُمْ صَدَقاتٍ): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr); «أشفقتم» is a verb and its fāʿil, i.e. did you fear? «أن» with what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar), accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "of giving", and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «أشفقتم»; it was also said that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The object of «تقدموا» is «صدقات», and the object of «أشفقتم» is omitted.
(فَإِذْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا وَتابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ فَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكاةَ وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ): the fāʾ is resumptive. On «إذ» there are several views:
1- That it is an adverb for past time, and the meaning is: you abandoned that in the past, so make up for it by performing the prayer and paying the zakat.
2- That it is an adverb in the sense of «إذا», like the saying of Allah the Exalted «إذ الأغلال في أعناقهم»; the discussion of it has preceded at length, so refer to it if you wish.
3- That it is in the sense of the conditional «إن».
«لم» is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; «تفعلوا» is an imperfect verb made jussive by «لم». «وتاب»: the wāw is circumstantial, resumptive or parenthetical, and the clause is parenthetical between the condition and its answer; «تاب الله» is a verb and its fāʿil; «عليكم» is attached to «تاب». The fāʾ is linking; «أقيموا الصلاة» is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi; «آتوا الزكاة» is conjoined to «فأقيموا الصلاة», and likewise His saying «وأطيعوا الله ورسوله».
(وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ): a mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause «تعملون» is the ṣila of «ما»; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «خبير».

* Rhetoric:
1- In the saying of Allah the Exalted «يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات» there is generalisation followed by specification. The detail of that is that the reward of raising ranks here is appropriate to the deed, because what was commanded is making room in the gatherings, so that they would not compete for nearness to the elevated place around him ﷺ and so crowd one another; that does not befit the manners of the gathering, the first of which is avoiding disturbing those sitting together and spoiling their clarity, and avoiding what muddies their serenity and troubles their minds. Since the one who complies with that command lowers himself from the elevation that is competed for, out of compliance and humility, he was rewarded for his humility by the raising of ranks. Then, since it was known that the people of knowledge are such that they deserve, in their own eyes and in the eyes of people, the elevation of their seats, He singled them out for mention at the reward, to make it easy for them to give up the elevation they have in the gathering out of humility toward Allah the Exalted. In this specification there is an allusion to the excellence of knowledge. It suffices us to cite the report of Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him: when he recited this verse he would say: "O people, understand this verse, and let it make you desire knowledge." And from him ﷺ: "Between the scholar and the worshipper are a hundred ranks; between every two ranks is the running distance of a trained racehorse for seventy years." And from him, upon him be blessing and peace: "Three will intercede on the Day of Resurrection: the prophets, then the scholars, then the martyrs." How great, then, is a rank between prophethood and martyrdom! And from al-Aḥnaf: "The scholars were almost lords; and every might not made firm by knowledge ends in abasement" [Translator's note: the source reads «فإلى ذلك ما يصير», apparently for «فإلى ذُلٍّ ما يصير»].
And since we are dealing with knowledge and its lofty rank, we must point to an eloquent subtle point, namely that when He singled out the scholars for the raising of ranks, He joined [them with the believers] because they combined knowledge and action [Translator's note: the sentence is elliptical in the source: «أنه قرن حين خصّ العلماء برفع الدرجات لما جمعوا بين العلم والعمل»]; for knowledge, despite the loftiness of its rank and the eminence of its station, requires action joined to it.
2- In His saying «بين يدي نجواكم» there is a metaphor drawn from one who has two hands. The verification of this metaphor has preceded in the verse of al-Ḥujurāt, so renew your acquaintance with it.
